mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed persistently elevated (+3.0 to +4.0) over the last four weeks, indicating households are sheltering in place; this behavioral inertia will continue to suppress discretionary retail and recreation trips over the next four weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC below its recent mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL positive and rising across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL remaining at or above +3.0 throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS rebound from -25.9 at t-1w to -15.7 at t-0w signals an early loosening of outdoor-movement restrictions; if this rebound continues past a threshold, retail and recreation footfall will follow with a lagged increase within two weeks as the same policy relaxation extends to markets and shops.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -25.9 to -15.7 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of PARKS sustaining a >8-point weekly increase for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed (around -24 to -26) while WORKPLACES stays near -8, jointly indicating that commuting and work-related trip chains that normally generate incidental retail visits are absent; the combined suppression of both series will keep RETAIL_REC flat-to-negative over the next four weeks because retail trips are largely unbundled from commuting.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days by more than 2 points even though both TRANSIT stays below -20 and WORKPLACES stays below -7 throughout.

mechanism_narrative: Delhi is in an active lockdown regime evidenced by stable deep declines in TRANSIT and PARKS; as long as this regime persists without an official relaxation signal, RETAIL_REC will remain within its current narrow band (-7 to -9) over the next week, showing no meaningful net change.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC ranged -7.1 to -8.9 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC moves outside the -5 to -11 band within one week while TRANSIT and PARKS remain at their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: The large single-week PARKS plunge at t-1w (-25.9) followed by partial recovery suggests a temporary enforcement crackdown that has since eased; if PARKS volatility of this magnitude recurs, it signals renewed enforcement intensity that will suppress RETAIL_REC within two weeks as similar restrictions extend to markets.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 15.3 points from t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks following a PARKS week-on-week drop exceeding 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-May heat in Delhi independently depresses outdoor PARKS visits regardless of policy, decoupling PARKS movements from retail demand; this seasonal effect implies PARKS-driven inferences about RETAIL_REC direction will be unreliable and RETAIL_REC will instead continue its own flat-to-slightly-declining four-week trend driven by heat-related reduced footfall to open-air markets.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and RETAIL_REC show divergent weekly patterns despite common seasonal exposure
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in step with any PARKS recovery during the next four weeks, contradicting the claimed seasonal decoupling.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 2.4 to 4.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even as GROCERY_PHARM continues rising for three or more consecutive weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between +3.0 and +4.0 while TRANSIT stayed between -24 and -26
regime_hint: hardened lockdown with synchronized residential and transit signals
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days without any corresponding easing (decline) in RESIDENTIAL or improvement in TRANSIT.
